trigger_main: validate untrusted input from HTTP request body query params headers
trigger_variants: accept JSON payload from API client
read user-supplied parameter from query string
guidance: Validate every input at the trust boundary (API edge, queue consumer entry, file ingest) — not deep in business logic. Use a schema/DTO layer that REJECTS malformed input before any handler runs. Treat ANY data crossing a trust boundary as hostile.
why: Deep-in-stack validation leaks malformed data into invariants the rest of the code assumes; boundary validation contains the blast radius and fails fast with a clear error. OWASP A03:2021 (Injection) and A04:2021 (Insecure Design) both root-cause to missing boundary checks.
alternatives_to_avoid: validating only what the current handler happens to touch
try/catch around business logic to swallow parse errors
trusting upstream-service contracts without re-validation at consumer

trigger_main: log request payload or response body or full exception object
guidance: Never log secrets, tokens, passwords, full PII, or raw request payloads. Define a redaction list (Authorization, Cookie, password, ssn, card-number, api-key, refresh-token, etc.) applied centrally in the logger middleware. Log structured key/value with the redacted shape, not free-form text.
why: Logs are durable, multi-region, often shared with vendors (Datadog, Sentry). One leaked token in a log line can leak everywhere logs are mirrored. OWASP A09:2021 (Security Logging and Monitoring Failures) and PCI-DSS 3.4 both forbid storing sensitive data in logs.
alternatives_to_avoid: printing the full incoming HTTP request for debugging in prod
logging stack trace that includes function-local variables in clear
logging password hash 'because it is hashed'

trigger_main: retry failed HTTP request or message handler or job
trigger_variants: cron job that may run twice
guidance: Make every operation that can be retried idempotent. Use a client-supplied idempotency key (X-Idempotency-Key header, message id, request id) and persist it with the result. On retry: short-circuit if the key was already processed, return the cached result. NEVER assume retries won't happen — networks, queues, and humans all generate dupes.
why: At-least-once delivery is the default in any distributed system (HTTP retries, SQS, Kafka, cron). Non-idempotent retry of a 'charge payment' or 'send email' causes user-visible failures: double-charges, duplicate emails. Stripe/Google/AWS all require idempotency keys for write APIs for this reason.
alternatives_to_avoid: assuming a successful 200 means the operation ran exactly once
relying on database unique constraint as the only dedup mechanism
retrying inside the same transaction without checking prior state

trigger_main: read config or env var at request handler time
trigger_variants: try/catch around getenv with default fallback
guidance: Validate ALL required configuration at process startup, BEFORE accepting any request. If a required secret/URL/flag is missing, log the missing key and exit non-zero. Do NOT use silent defaults for connection strings, API keys, or feature flags that change behavior. A misconfigured process must crash, not silently degrade.
why: Silent fallback at request time turns a deploy bug into a slow leak: some requests succeed (warm cache), others fail mysteriously when they hit the missing key. Crashing at startup makes the failure visible to deploy tooling and rollbacks can fire. 12-Factor App III (Config) and Google SRE 'crash-only software' both prescribe this.
alternatives_to_avoid: try/catch wrap around config read that logs and continues
reading config inside the hot path on every request

trigger_main: log error or info message with concatenated string
guidance: Log structured key/value (JSON or logfmt), never free-form interpolated strings. Each log line should have a stable schema: level, timestamp, message, trace_id, plus typed fields (user_id, request_id, duration_ms, etc.). String-concatenated logs are unsearchable, ungroupable, and break log aggregation tools.
why: Free-form logs force grep-and-pray when an incident happens. Structured logs enable filter-by-field, percentile metrics, and tracing-correlation across services. Every major observability stack (Datadog, Splunk, Elastic, Loki) is built around structured ingestion. Google SRE 'Observability' chapter prescribes this.
alternatives_to_avoid: concatenating values into the message string for the log call
logging a JSON-stringified object as the message field
